Slater made three changes to his team for the must-win Origin II at the MCG, with Broncos superstar Reece Walsh named on the bench after not playing since the 2024 series loss.

Walsh was overlooked completely for the series opener in Sydney and his recall comes despite indifferent form during Brisbane's miserable five-game losing streak.

"We think it's the best thing for the footy team [to have him] on the bench there," Slater said.

"We all know what Reece is capable of.

Reece Walsh has been named on an extended bench despite indifferent club form. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

"He's built a really good game and if needed I'm sure he'll go out there and perform that."

Most of the questions at Slater's press conference surrounded Walsh, with the coach refusing to elaborate on what precipitated the return to the side, saying he would keep it "in-house".

"It's about us playing our best football as a footy team," he said.

"We're more than one person and that's been the strength of this team for a long time.

"We're more than one person, one player. The strength of the team is the team and that's what we'll be going after."

Look back at the announcement and Slater's press conference in our live blog below.

Live updates Queensland's State of Origin II team confirmed J By Jon Healy Here's the full 20-man squad: Kalyn Ponga Selwyn Cobbo Robert Toia Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow Jojo Fifita Cameron Munster (c) Sam Walker Thomas Flegler Harry Grant Tino Fa'asuamaleaui Briton Nikora Kurt Capewell Reuben Cotter Max Plath Lindsay Collins Kulikefu Finefeuiaki * Trent Loiero Reece Walsh * Murray Taulagi * Heilum Luki * * Did not play Game I Collapse all posts off Sort Sort posts Latest Select an option New: Filters Choose what information you see below by using filters Filter Posts All 19 Key Events 7 Comments 1 We'll sign off there J By Jon Healy So that's that. The Maroons are largely as expected with Pat Carrigan's injury forcing a reshuffle in the forwards, while Reece Walsh is named on an extended bench. ABC Sport will be live blogging the NRL game between the Bulldogs and Eels from 4:05pm AEST, after which NSW coach Laurie Daley will reveal his team for State of Origin II. Then, of course, it will be game time before you know it at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Wednesday, June 17. We'll be live for every moment, so please join us then. Maroons 'more than one person': Slater J By Jon Healy Obviously Billy Slater was asked a lot of questions about Reece Walsh this morning. Loading... He didn't really shed any light on what Walsh has done to earn selection since missing Game I, nor did he say what his plan was for the electric and erratic fullback, constantly trying to steer the conversation back to the team. "We know what he's capable of. It's about us playing our best football as a footy team. "We're more than one person and that's been the strength of this team for a long time. "We're more than one person, one player. The strength of the team is the team and that's what we'll be going after." Queensland's woeful MCG record J By Jon Healy Melbourne played host to one of the Maroons' greatest Origin moments, when Darren Lockyer's intercept in the 2006 decider kicked off the eight-straight streak. But that was at Docklands. Down the road at the MCG, Queensland has only won one State of Origin game. Here's how it's played out: 2024 — Game II: NSW 38-18

NSW 38-18 2018 — Game I: NSW 22-12

NSW 22-12 2015 — Game II: NSW 30-18

NSW 30-18 1997 — Game II: NSW 15-14

NSW 15-14 1995 — Game II: Qld 20-12

Qld 20-12 1994 — Game II: NSW 14-0

NSW 14-0 1990 — Game II: NSW 12-6 After using Paul Vautin's 1995 "Nobodies" side as inspiration during last year's series win, Billy Slater says he might have to give him a call again this time around. "Might have to give Fatty a call," he says, adding it's not overly relevant to his team in 2026. "We can look back all we want but unless we focus on right now and the future, results will be what the last 30 years have been. "Really important we focus on the now and chase our performance." Slater to play peacemaker between playmakers J By Jon Healy Cameron Munster seemed to go after Maroons teammate Kalyn Ponga in the Storm's win over the Knights on Friday. The pair came together on a number of occasions, with Munster at one point whacking Ponga after an error, sparking a melee between the teams. (Supplied: Kayo) Slater insists the camaraderie will be there now that game is over, but maybe a bonding session is called for. "They'll be all good. They're both competitive," he says. "I know Cameron Munster really well, I'm sure they would've had a laugh about it afterwards. "It's a game of footy; They're all out there to compete and do their best. Might have to put 'em together the first couple of days." Smiling Selwyn back again J By Jon Healy After missing games last year and getting let go by the Broncos after a run of bad form, Selwyn Cobbo is on fire in 2026 for the Dolphins and was one of the Queensland's best in Origin I. "Selwyn's more mature. The biggest thing with Selwyn is he looks happy. He's smiling when he plays for the Dolphins, he's smiling when he plays for Queensland," Slater says. "He's in an environment where he's happy, wants to work hard and wants to go after his game." Slater says Cobbo is only 23 years old (he actually turned 24 a couple of days ago) but it's still remarkable considering how long it feels like he's been around. Trying to make sense of Game I J By Jon Healy Slater says the series opener, such as it was, was a tough game to assess when coming to the selection table this time around. "It's a bit of a balance of celebrating and keeping a hold of what we did well and then going after incremental improvements. "I think traditional Game II and III are improved performances by both teams and we'll be looking to chase that, but first and foremost we'll be looking to chase what we got right in Game I." Slater on handing a debut to Kulikefu Finefeuiaki J By Jon Healy Slater says the phone call to Kulikefu Finefeuiaki was one of the best parts of the job. "He's been playing the standard of footy that is acceptable for this footy team for a long time. "He's worked really hard. "Looking forward to getting him out there in a Queensland jersey and getting his game on." Slater says he's always run the ball hard, but his defence has improved this year, which has seen him elevated. Billy Slater explains Reece Walsh's selection J By Jon Healy Maroons coach Billy Slater says he is going to work out Reece Walsh's exact role in the team over the next 10 days. "We think it's the best thing for the footy team [to have him] on the bench there. "We all know what Reece is capable of." Slater says he's not going to reveal what he's seen in Walsh the past few weeks or the conversations he's had with him. "I'll keep all that stuff in-house. I've got a great relationship with Reece. He's built a really good game and if needed I'm sure he'll go out there and perform that." What role will Reece Walsh play in Origin II? J By Jon Healy (Getty) If everything goes to plan, I'd wager none. In this team, Reece Walsh feels like a "break glass in case of emergency" kinda guy. If the Maroons are down 10 with 15 minutes left, I wouldn't be surprised if he comes onto the field alongside Kalyn Ponga, with Walsh out the back and Ponga playing a link role through the middle. Injury-wise, I think he's only really there to cover Ponga if he goes down. Any other outside back position you'd think would be covered by Murray Taulagi. I'd say we can expect more answers from Billy Slater during his press conference at 9:30am AEST, but I don't think he'll reveal too much there. The changes for the Maroons J By Jon Healy (Getty) The most substantive changes to Billy Slater's Queensland team have been brought about by Pat Carrigan's ankle injury, which will see him miss the rest of the series. Carrigan came off the bench early to replace Tom Flegler in Game I and made way for Trent Loiero for the final 15 minutes. Starting lock Max Plath subbed off for Briton Nikora to come on in the back row, shifting Reuben Cotter to lock, where he will start Game II. Plath has shifted to the bench to give Slater some utility off the bench. Speaking of the bench, Kulikefu Finefeuiaki is set to make his debut after being named in the extended squad a couple of weeks ago, while Reece Walsh and sensational Origin performer Murray Taulagi replace Ezra Mam (benched by the Broncos) and Gehamat Shibasaki's (injured) spots. Walsh's woes J By Jon Healy Jon after watching Walsh yesterday he needs work on defence. He’s great when he has the ball in open space no question. One more thing as a fullback he must follow the ball when the other team is within 20m of his line. Thanks. - Robbo Hi Robbo, Reece Walsh has certainly been a mixed bag in 2026, and here are his stats during Brisbane's current five-game losing streak against the Roosters, Manly, Warriors, Dragons and Titans. 1 try

4 try assists

1 line break

22 tackle breaks

135.8 avg run metres

12 errors

6 penalties/set restarts conceded It's been a rough trot. Queensland's team for the series opener J By Jon Healy As a reminder, here is how the Maroons lined up for Game I: Kalyn Ponga Selwyn Cobbo Rob Toia Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow Jojo Fifita Cameron Munster Sam Walker Tom Flegler Harry Grant Tino Fa'asuamaleaui Reuben Cotter Kurt Capewell Max Plath Briton Nikora Lindsay Collins Pat Carrigan * Trent Loiero Ezra Mam ^ Gehamat Shibasaki *^ Kulikefu Finefeauiaki ^ * Unavailable for Game II ^ Did not take the field in Game I Reece Walsh admitted he hadn't been up to Origin standard J By Jon Healy (Getty) Reece Walsh's first two Origin games as a 20-year-old in 2023 were phenomenal. Later that year, he sparked the Broncos within a couple minutes of a premiership, then struggled in 2024 and early in 2025, during which he was snubbed for selection for Origin III, before leading Brisbane to grand final glory with one of the greatest runs we've ever seen by an NRL player. But this year has been another rocks-and-diamonds type season from the mercurial fullback, who admitted on Wednesday his form hadn't warranted an Origin call-up. "I know the standards it takes to play for Queensland and I'm honest with myself. I probably haven't been living up to those standards," he said. "That's what makes [State of Origin] so great. Once you put that [Maroons] jersey on, you know what it takes to get back there. I'm a realist and I understand I haven't been upholding those standards." Now, if he wasn't good enough for a bench spot in Game I, I'm not sure what his performances in Brisbane's woeful losses to the Dragons and Titans did to convince Billy Slater he was ready now. Maybe Slater just wants a Walsh with something to prove. What happened in Origin I? J By Jon Healy Just as a little reminder of how Origin I played out: The Blues were woeful to start and the Maroons made them pay to the tune of 20-0 inside 20 minutes. After weathering that storm, the game settled down before all hell broke loose when Kalyn Ponga hit Tolu Koula with a shoulder charge on 57 minutes. Referee Ashley Klein overruled the bunker to send the Queensland fullback off and, despite a mighty defensive effort with 12 men in the rain, the Blues won courtesy of James Tedesco's leap, catch, bobble and put-down with 90 seconds left. For more detail, go relive it in our live blog. Maroons let 20-0 lead slip in Origin I after Kalyn Ponga sent off late Why was Reece Walsh left out of Origin I? J By Jon Healy It may seem odd considering the way he finished 2025, but Reece Walsh hasn't played State of Origin since the Maroons' loss in the 2024 decider. Due to a series of circumstances, he hasn't actually played the final minutes of an Origin victory since the 2023 series opener. We broke down Billy Slater's Game I decision, and it's worth revisiting as reports emerge that Walsh is back in the frame for a bench spot this time around. For the second straight game, Slater has overlooked Walsh. But why? When are the Blues naming their team? J By Jon Healy NSW coach Laurie Daley will reveal his team after this afternoon's King's Birthday clash between Canterbury and Parramatta. Queensland was never likely to have any stake in that game in terms of players, so it makes sense for them to get the Maroons into camp ASAP, but Daley will be keeping a close eye on Bulldogs centre Stephen Crichton from 4:05pm. (Getty) Crichton has started every game at centre since Origin II 2022, but has battled to start this year, is struggling with a shoulder injury and was uncharacteristically poor in Game I. With Kotoni Staggs, Latrell Mitchell, Casey McLean and Tolu Koula just some of the names in the mix, Crichton needs to impress and show no signs of ill health this afternoon. When is Queensland naming its team? J By Jon Healy The official announcement is set for 9am (AEST), although they jumped the gun for the Game I team. After the team is revealed, Queensland coach Billy Slater will hold a press conference from 9:30am. We'll bring you all of that live. Welcome to Team List … Monday J By Jon Healy Hello and welcome to ABC Sport's live coverage of the announcement of Queensland's team for State of Origin II. The Maroons are naming their squad for the second game at the MCG after surrendering a 20-0 lead to lose the series opener in Sydney. That means it's must-win territory for Queensland now, so what will Billy Slater do? World.title: Aussie pole vaulter hands Duplantis first loss in more than 1,000 days
World.content:
Australian pole vaulter Kurtis Marschall has pulled off a major upset, defeating world record holder Armand "Mondo" Duplantis at the Stockholm Diamond League meet.

Marschall handed Sweden's two-time Olympic champion his first loss in more than 1,000 days when he cleared 5.90 metres to clinch victory.

Duplantis could only manage a successful clearance of 5.80m to place second, well short of his world record mark of 6.31m.

"I can't believe it, I'm going to cherish this for my whole life," said Marschall, a two-time world championships bronze medallist.

"They don't come easy in this day and age.

"I jumped great in these conditions, I'm very happy, but I know Mondo isn't going to let it happen in the future.

"This stadium wouldn't be what it is without him, so to come here and to do it in front of this crowd, I'm cherishing every single moment.

"He's one of the best competitors and one of the best blokes. I love him with all my heart."

Armand Duplantis (right) speaks with Kurtis Marschall during the men's pole vault competition. (Getty Images: David Lidstrom)

Duplantis, who has set the men's pole vault record 15 times, had won 40 consecutive events.

"Big hats off to Kurtis today, he was the better man and he beat me fair and square," Duplantis said.

"I have no excuses."

Australian teammates Matthew Denny and Cameron Myers also recorded podium finishes in Stockholm.

Olympic bronze medallist Denny was second in the men's discus with a best throw of 69.02m.

Sweden's reigning world champion Daniel Stahl won with 69.60m.

"I felt there was more to give and maybe I got a bit greedy on the last couple of rounds trying to get that bigger distance," Denny said.

"But it was a great competition and I'm really finding some good stuff that will be kind to me later in the season."

Myers was also second in his event, the men's 1,500m.

The Canberran stopped the clock in 3:30.32 to finish behind US Olympic bronze medallist Yared Nuguse (3:30.11).

"It's not the outcome that I wanted but you have to play to how you feel on the day, and I didn't feel great, which is frustrating," Myers said.

World.title: Aussies crowned rugby sevens world champions after conquering NZ
World.content:
Maddison Levi has defied a knee injury to score a superb double as Australia wrapped up the women's rugby sevens World Championship in Bordeaux, France.

Australia defeated New Zealand 26-19 in the final to clinch the world title.

New Zealand won the first of the three World Championship tournaments in Hong Kong, before Australia secured back-to-back triumphs in Valladolid and Bordeaux.

Levi was injured during the Valladolid tournament and was kept under wraps for the first two days of competition in Bordeaux until the semis and final.

She produced a player-of-the-match display in the final with two tries, while Heidi Dennis and Faith Nathan also crossed the stripe to help Australia secure a third overall title in five years.

Levi also saved a try in defence, when she chased down New Zealand's Katelyn Vaha'akolo during the second half.

Maddison Levi starred for Australia in the final against New Zealand. (Reuters: Catherine Steenkeste)

"It's pretty surreal," Levi said after the final.

"The girls helped me get back and I wouldn't be here without them. We spoke before the game that it's been our most consistent season, and we've been in every final.

"We've beaten an amazing New Zealand side. It's always hard when we play them.

"No matter even when we beat them, it's always a tough game."

Aussie 7s star has 'unfinished business' For an athlete still in the early stages of her professional career, Australian rugby 7s player Kaitlin Shave has already experienced the highs and lows of sport.

Levi's sister Teagan also enjoyed a big tournament, while co-captain Bella Nasser came up trumps with a big defensive play early in the final.

Earlier on the final day, the Tim Walsh-coached side reached the tournament decider with a 21-7 victory over USA in the semis.

"In the end, our big-game players all stepped up and the depth in our program means we have more than one player capable of turning a game at any moment," Walsh said.

"Champions are not stars. Champions are team players that consistently show up and perform even when they don't feel like it."

The overall men's world title went to South Africa, despite the team being defeated in the semis in Bordeaux by hosts France, who went on to beat New Zealand 14-5 in the final.

The Australian men ended up fifth in the season's standings, winning their last match of the season 29-0 against Great Britain to claim seventh position in Bordeaux.

AAP

World.title: Zverev claims first major with French Open victory
World.content:
Alexander Zverev has finally won his first major title after grinding down Flavio Cobolli in the men's French Open final.

Zverev had been runner-up at a major three times in his career, but he broke through with a 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7, (5-7), 6-1 defeat of the stubborn Coboli after four hours and 16 minutes on Court Philippe ‌Chatrier.

He capped a relentless run by becoming the first German man to win a major title since Boris Becker's Australian Open triumph in 1996.

Andreeva wins French Open Mirra Andreeva defeats surprise finalist Maja Chwalińska 6-3, 6-2 to become the youngest French Open champion in more than three decades.

In a ‌Paris fortnight during which Carlos Alcaraz was absent due to injury and Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic lost early to blow the draw wide open, the second seed embraced his new status as the favourite for the Musketeers' cup and delivered.

"I want to congratulate Flavio. What an unbelievable two weeks, reaching your first grand slam final, ‌and playing your first final like this," Zverev said in his on-court interview.

"From the bottom of my heart, I hope you lift this trophy very soon. ⁠You're one of the best people on tour.

"I really felt the crowd was pushing me throughout these ‌two weeks and without you guys I wouldn't have won this tournament."

With the sun shining at Roland-Garros, Zverev broke Cobolli with a backhand shot that pinged off the Italian's orange-framed racquet, and he tightened his grip further to wrap up the opening set with a forehand winner down the middle.

Cobolli fired himself up and produced stunning shot-making to break in the seventh game of the next set and then drew level with a confident hold, as the centre court crowd whipped up a football-like atmosphere for the former AS Roma academy player.

Those ‌voices soon fell silent deep in the third set as 10th seed Cobolli struck a forehand into the net to gift Zverev a set point.

Zverev promptly regained the advantage thanks to another unforced error.

A spell of passive play from Zverev meant he was broken twice ⁠in the fourth set, but the 2024 French Open runner-up dialled up the intensity to go level ‌at 5-5, only to crack under pressure in ‌the tiebreak as Cobolli fired a forehand rocket to force a decider.

With the closing stages of the contest lacking the quality of last year's epic between Alcaraz ‌and Sinner, Zverev edged in front and used all his experience to finally earn his long-awaited crown.

Alexander Zverev was overcome with emotion after sealing victory. (Getty Images: Dan Istitene)

Zverev dropped to the floor and sobbed, before dusting himself off to greet his close friend Cobolli and then soak up the applause at a venue in ‌which he has tasted joy and sorrow.

He left the ⁠2022 tournament in a wheelchair after seriously injuring his ankle in the semifinals against Rafa Nadal.

"This court is so special to me in so many ways," Zverev said.

"Some of the best moments of my life have happened on this court, and some of the worst too. I sat here with seven broken bones four years ago, and I lost a final here."

Flavio Cobolli was left frustrated during key moments of the final. (Getty Images: Dan Istitene)

Cobolli was left to rue a missed chance ⁠to return the Roland-Garros men's title to Italy for the first time in 50 years after Adriano Panatta defeated American Harold Solomon in the 1976 title clash.

"If someone asked me who deserved this title more, I would always say you. It's been an honour, through our relationship, to share the court today," Coboli said.

"I'm happy for you, but I'm also sad, because I was close, and I feel it now. You achieved your dream.

"Let me win the next time."

Reuters

Tech.title: WWDC protesters want Apple to ban Elon Musk’s apps
Tech.content:
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Apple’s big developer conference is today, and protesters are using the occasion to call on the company to remove “nudify apps” from the App Store and pull “known” child sexual abuse material from iCloud.

Outside the visitor’s center at Apple’s Cupertino campus, protesters have put up a large sign saying: “Apple is powered by child sexual abuse” and asking incoming CEO John Ternus “What will you do?” The protesters come from UltraViolet, a women’s advocacy group, and Heat Initiative, a group that aims to “hold tech companies accountable for enabling and profiting from child sexual abuse.”

Apple and Google came under significant scrutiny earlier this year for continuing to keep apps like xAI’s Grok on their app stores even though users were able to make nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes. In pamphlets distributed at the protest, the organizations say that “at least 47 nudify apps have been found on Apple’s App Store” and that “Apple has made an estimated $117 million minimum from nudify apps,” including “an estimated $35+ million from Grok alone,” citing data from the Tech Transparency Project. UltraViolet also has a website dedicated to its protest today.

Photo by Allison Johnson / The Verge

Apple previously scrapped plans to scan photos saved to iCloud for child sexual abuse imagery over privacy concerns.

Apple didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

Tech.title: WWDC 2026 live blog: On the ground at Apple’s keynote
Tech.content:
It’s conference season! Today, we’re back at Apple Park in Cupertino, California, for Apple’s annual developer keynote. Unlike other conferences, there’s a distinct rhythm to WWDC. We know we’re going to get a peek at everything coming to iOS 27, macOS 27, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27 — basically all the “Class of ’27” operating systems. As for what those updates will entail? Given the “All Systems Glow” tagline, probably a lot of Apple Intelligence. After all, in the lead-up to the event, the rumor mill has been buzzing that we may see Apple take another run at an AI Siri.

The pressure is particularly high this year. This will be Tim Cook’s final WWDC as CEO before handing over the reins to John Ternus, so everyone will be hungry for any hint of what the forthcoming era will look like. Will we see Liquid Glass refinements? Perhaps iOS 27 updates that nod at a foldable iPhone? A video featuring Craig Federighi’s hair? (We’re most confident about that last one.)

One thing we’re not expecting is new hardware — though you can’t fully rule out a surprise M5 refresh. However, Apple’s already had several launches this year, including the MacBook Neo, iPhone 17e, and AirTag 2. Plus there are RAM shortages to consider, and the company tends to save its core product launches for its September event.

The keynote will kick off at 10AM PT / 1PM ET. You can watch and follow along here for minute-by-minute updates.

Tech.title: NotebookLM’s Gemini 3.5 upgrade adds a cloud computer and help finding sources
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Google is rolling out “across the board” updates to NotebookLM. The AI-powered note-taking app now uses Google’s upgraded Gemini 3.5 model, which will allow it to respond with “more accurate and reliable information,” according to a blog post on Monday.

Launched in 2023, NotebookLM allows you to interact with your notes and sources using AI, as well as ask questions about the materials. With this update, Google says you can start a research project by just asking NotebookLM questions about a topic, instead of importing notes or YouTube videos. NotebookLM will use Google Search to help you find relevant sources, building on its “discover” feature to help you find useful resources on the web.

You can choose which sources found by NotebookLM to import. Image: Google

Additionally, NotebookLM now runs on Google’s agentic coding platform, Antigravity. Each notebook within the app is connected to a “secure cloud computer,” enabling NotebookLM to write and run code to help with your research. NotebookLM can also output information in new formats and file types, including PDF documents, data visualizations (PNG, SVG), Nano Banana-generated images (PNG, JPG, GIF), Excel and PowerPoint files, CSV sheets, and more.

This update is coming to users on Google’s AI Ultra plan and Workspace customers, but the company plans to expand it to more plans in the future.

The Pro 6E was Eero’s top-end mesh Wi-Fi router back in 2022, and it’s still a solid pick if you want fast, reliable Wi-Fi coverage around your multi-room or multi-story abode. It can also deliver beyond gigabit wired speeds if your internet plan supports it. Ahead of Prime Day 2026, Amazon and Best Buy have knocked down the cost of a three-pack, matching its best-ever price that we last saw ahead of the holidays in December 2025.

There are so, so many different Wi-Fi routers to choose between, and it’s confusing. The Eero Pro 6E tick a good number of boxes. For one, each tri-band router supports 2.4, 5, and 6GHz bands, meaning smart home tech won’t have an issue connecting to lower bands, nor will newer devices that can run unencumbered on the 6GHz band. Eero routers are known for being simple to setup, which is handy if you don’t know anything about home networking.

While each router can broadcast a speedy wireless signal (up to 1.3Gbps) across 2,000 square feet, routers furthest away from the modem will experience speed degradation. It’s normal across all mesh Wi-Fi systems, regardless of brand. Thankfully, the Pro 6E supports wired backhaul at 1Gbps speeds, letting you connect each of the Pro 6E nodes together via Ethernet to address it.
